own_solution.law: For a pipe closed at one end, f = c/(4L_eff). Constant effective length gives f_301 = 440 sqrt(301/288) = 449.820952 Hz. The beat frequency is |f_301 - 440|.
assumptions: The pipe sounds in its fundamental longitudinal acoustic mode.
The explicitly stated 440 Hz is the fork frequency when the pipe is tuned.

TC352.regime: Linear acoustics: displacement is much smaller than the wavelength and oscillatory air speed is much smaller than sound speed. At 18 μm, the acoustic Mach number is approximately 0.00015.

T096C.regime: Linear acoustics: displacement is much smaller than the wavelength and oscillatory air speed is much smaller than sound speed. At 18 μm, the acoustic Mach number is approximately 0.00015.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The pitch-increment variants do not preserve the stated quantity: T54B8 and T41CC specify only a 'small amount', whereas their corresponding numerical renderings T3EBE and T056D specify 62 Hz.

counterexamples: For T9D97 or TFAFF, a fork raised from 378 Hz to 440 Hz before tuning satisfies the explicit tuning condition and gives 9.820952 Hz beats; adding 62 Hz to the stated 440 Hz instead would give 11.204813 Hz beats but would require changing the explicit tuning frequency.
notes: The base problem is well-posed. Assignments for T9D97 and TFAFF follow the literal chronology: the fork has its explicitly stated frequency of 440 Hz when tuning occurs, so an earlier adjustment supplies historical information without changing the answer. These sentences invite a competing perturbation reading in which 440 Hz becomes 502 Hz, but that reading conflicts with the stated tuning condition. Earlier-experiment fork adjustments likewise do not determine the present frequency. End correction enters L_eff = L_physical + correction, but tuning fixes L_eff and eliminates its separate dependence from the frequency ratio. The amplitude variants preserve 18 μm, and the end-correction variants preserve 2.3 cm. No explicit minimal-pair identifiers are supplied; the rendering defect concerns the instruction that variants of the same quantity preserve its number and unit.
